applicability: SGLang scheduler calls with reqs_to_exclude=None or [] (the common no-exclusions path). Benefit scales with len(self.reqs) and filter frequency. No effect on the nonempty-exclusions path or when an explicit keep_indices list is supplied.

cpu_tests.limitations: Stdlib-only unit-level test that AST-extracts and executes the actual production keep_indices block with fake Req objects. It imports no torch/CUDA and does not exercise the full scheduler, tokenizer, model execution, or end-to-end generation, and it does not measure wall-clock speedup. Nonempty-path equality semantics are checked with unhashable fake requests to rule out set/hashability changes.

requested_measurement.small_c1_first: Run the small C1 scheduler-overhead comparison first under the fixed policy: same host, Python build, workload, and batch sizes; compare ScheduleBatch.filter_batch CPU time for reqs_to_exclude in {None, []} before vs after this commit, reporting per-call CPU time and call counts. This probes Python scheduler overhead only.
requested_measurement.larger_c_only_if_justified: Escalate to larger C/batch sizes only if the small C1 comparison shows a repeatable reduction that clears run-to-run variance; otherwise stop and make no benefit claim.

risks: Touches a hot scheduler function; intended behavior is equivalent, but full scheduler integration is not exercised in this environment.
Any real speedup is likely small and may sit within measurement noise; no GPU-side effect is expected or claimed.
Nonempty exclusions must retain list membership and unhashable/equality semantics; covered by runtime and AST checks in the CPU regression.
No GPU, SSH, benchmark harness, or official scorer was available here; official evaluation by the trusted controller is required.
learning: Empty-list membership probes in a per-request Python comprehension are redundant and can be hoisted behind a truthiness check without changing list membership, equality, or hashability semantics for nonempty exclusions. Round 1 produced no production change (error_max_turns); this round kept scope to one function, one AST-extracted CPU regression, and an honest measurement request.
